title: measurements.json
description: Output of scripts/scan.mjs. Documentation only: nothing validates against it. This file lists the fields that every scan writes. Measures add their own sections (for example security or context), and each one extends this file. Outside meta, no value holds an absolute path of the machine that ran the scan; paths are relative to the target and use forward slashes.

meta.description: Values that depend on the machine or on the time. Determinism checks ignore this key.

tool.description: Tool name and version from package.json, written as name@version.

scannedAt.description: UTC time of the scan, in ISO 8601.

targetRoot.description: Absolute path of the scanned folder, as the scanner resolved it. It is the only absolute path of this machine in the file, and the findings validator uses it to read the evidence.

isRepo.description: True when git lists the files of the target folder.

head.description: Full object name of HEAD, or null when there is no commit.

fileListSource.description: git when git listed the files; walk when the folder was read from disk.

fileCount.description: Number of files in the list.

inventory.description: Harness files. Added by measures; sorted by path. One item per path.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target.

kind.description: What the file is. memory: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or an import of one of them; rule: a file of .claude/rules/.

loadMode.description: When Claude Code loads the file. always: at the start of every session (counted in the budget); on-demand: when a related file is read or the skill is invoked; not-loaded: not loaded by default.

loadReason.description: Short English reason for loadMode. For an import it names the importing file.

lines.description: Number of lines. Null when the file was not read (memory files in subfolders, files over 4 MiB).

estTokens.description: Estimate with chars/4, labelled with estMethod. Null when the file was not read.

warnings.description: Things that were skipped or could not be read. Sorted by path, reason, source and detail; duplicates removed.

source.description: "fs" for file reads, "git" for the file list, or the id of the measure that reported it.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target, or "." for the target itself.

reason.description: Fixed code, such as outside-root, too-large or binary. The duplication measure writes code-file-too-large, code-file-minified and code-file-unreadable (its detail is the safe-fs reason) for a code file it skips, and code-files-cut or code-bytes-cut for the files that a cap cut.

detail.description: Optional fixed code with more context, never a message from the system. The structure measure writes count=N with the entries it cut, and the duplication measure writes count=N with the files or bytes it cut.

measuredFindings.description: Findings of the measured MVP rules. Written after the measures by the derive step (scripts/lib/measured-findings.mjs), from these measurements only; the target is never read again. Ids mf-N follow the order of EMITTERS (axis order), then the order of the measurements inside each emitter. A finding's impact is the highest impact of its triggers; its measurementRef is the ref of its first trigger with that impact, except for CTX-01 and COD-01, whose ref is their number. Each trigger has its own measurementRef. Impacts follow the thresholds in THRESHOLDS, which are provisional.

candidates.description: What the agent reads for the judgment rules. Not findings. Carry paths relative to the target and line numbers, never code text. Ids cand-N follow the order of the list: duplication groups (COD-01, COD-04), then hook scripts sorted by path (SEC-02, SEC-04), then memory and rule files in inventory order (RUL-01, RUL-02, RUL-03, VER-01, SEC-04, SEC-05, STR-01, COD-04).

undeterminable.description: Cases that a measured rule could not decide, with the reason. Never findings. In the order of EMITTERS, then the order of the measurements.

reason.description: What is undeterminable and the reason the measure gives.

context.description: Context that Claude Code loads at the start of a session. Measures add items to the shared lists; the core sets the total and the method.

ancestors.description: Memory files of the parent folders of the target that exist, by existence and size only: their content is never read. Paths are relative to the target (for example ../CLAUDE.md). Not in the inventory and not in the budget.

imports.description: Every @path import of a loaded memory file, sorted by from, line and ref. Imports inside fenced code blocks and code spans are not listed. Imports from rules are not listed.

from.description: The importing file, relative to the target.

ref.description: The text after @, redacted. "<outside>" for an absolute path that is not inside the target.

path.description: The root-relative path the import names, or null when it is external.

depth.description: Hop of the import: the importing file's depth plus one. The root memory file is depth 0. An import at depth 5 is too-deep and is not read.

status.description: ok: the file exists and is loaded (once). broken: missing or not a file. external: home path, absolute path outside the target, or a path that leaves the target; never read. too-deep: more than four hops. cycle: the file is one of the files that led to this import.

limits.description: Limits that the memory files break, sorted by path.

limit.description: memory-lines: an always-loaded file over 200 lines. memory-bytes: a memory file over 4 MiB, which is skipped.

estTokensTotal.description: Sum of the estTokens of byComponent. An estimate, labelled with estMethod.

estMethod.description: Estimation method. The only one; reports always show it next to the estimate.

byComponent.description: One item per component of the always-loaded budget, sorted by component. Measures add their components here; each component appears once.

component.description: Fixed name: skills, commands, subagents, or memory.

items.description: Files that make up the component, sorted by path.

unknownStatic.description: Items that enter the context but whose size cannot be known without running them, sorted. Not counted in estTokensTotal.

kind.description: mcp-server: a server of .mcp.json; hook-output: a hook whose stdout enters the context.

source.description: The file that declares the item.

instructions.description: What the memory files mention, checked against the target (brokenRefs, externalRefs), and the package manager that the target declares (packageManager). The lists are sorted by file, line and text; file is relative to the target. Texts are redacted (no absolute path of this machine).

brokenRefs.description: Paths and script commands that the memory files mention and the target does not have. Paths in code spans may exist from the root or from the folder of the memory file; links only from their own folder.

text.description: The text as written: the code span, the link target, or the command.

kind.description: path: inline code; link: Markdown link or image; script: npm, pnpm, yarn or bun script call.

reason.description: not-found: no file or folder; missing-script: the root package.json has no such script; no-package-json: the target has no package.json.

script.description: The script name. Only for kind script.

externalRefs.description: Paths that are not checked: absolute paths, home paths and relative paths that leave the target. Never stat-ed or read.

packageManager.description: The package manager that the target declares, compared with its lockfiles and with the managers that the memory text names. Only file names are read; no lockfile is opened.

field.description: The packageManager string of the root package.json, redacted; null when there is none.

fieldManager.description: The name before @ in field, when it is one of the four managers.

lockfiles.description: Lockfiles at the root, by name, sorted by path.

mentions.description: Whole-word names of a manager in the memory text, in prose and code: one entry per manager, file and line. Sorted by file, line and manager.

conflict.description: True when the field, the lockfiles and the mentions name more than one manager in total.

security.description: Security-relevant configuration. permissions is read as written; destructiveCoverage simulates the rules against the commands of the data file; secrets names secret files and masks literal secrets. Nothing is run and nothing is enforced.

permissions.description: Permission rules of the project settings files (shared and local). Lists are merged across both files and sorted. Values are redacted (no absolute path of this machine).

defaultMode.description: The defaultMode of the file with the higher precedence (local over shared), or null.

effect.description: auto and bypassPermissions are ignored when a project file sets them; default (also written manual), acceptEdits, plan and dontAsk apply.

disableBypassPermissionsMode.description: The value from the file with the higher precedence, or null. Docs: it works from any settings file.

destructiveCoverage.description: The commands of data/destructive-commands.json simulated against the project rules, defaultMode and PreToolUse hooks (permissions.mjs). Nothing runs: an outcome says what the configuration decides, not what a hook would do.

mode.description: The project defaultMode as claude-config parsed it (value, source, effect), or null. The outcomes use its value.

commands.description: One item per command of the data file, in the order of the file.

tool.description: The Claude Code tool that runs the command. cmd commands run inside PowerShell.

parts.description: The simple commands of a compound command.

insideProject.description: The example acts inside the project.

criticalPath.description: The example's target is a critical path.

builtInProtection.description: What Claude Code protects on its own for this kind of command, or null.

decidedBy.description: What decides the outcome: { kind: rule, list, rule, source }, { kind: mode, mode, ignoredMode? } or { kind: critical-path }. Null when nothing does.

preToolUseHook.description: Whether at least one PreToolUse hook runs for the command.

preToolUseHooks.description: Each PreToolUse hook whose matcher can cover Bash or PowerShell, in the order of claudeConfig.hooks.

if.description: The permission rule that filters the calls the hook runs for, or null.

tools.description: The shell tools that the matcher covers, or undeterminable when the matcher is an invalid regular expression.

subagents.description: Each subagent with a name, a permissionMode and a shell tool (from tools and disallowedTools), with the outcome of each command that it can run.

effectiveMode.description: The mode the subagent runs in (docs: sub-agents), or undeterminable when auto may apply.

ignoredMode.description: The subagent's own permissionMode, when that value does not apply. Absent otherwise.

secrets.description: Secret files and literal secrets. Secret files are named only: their content is never read. Every secret value is masked (a prefix, an ellipsis and the last four characters), and no raw value appears in any output.

fileListSource.description: git: the listed files are versioned. walk: the listed files are present on disk, versioned or not.

files.description: Files of the list whose base name is secret-shaped, sorted by path. Named only.

kind.description: Id of the file-name rule in data/secret-patterns.json.

literals.description: Secrets found in harness files only, sorted by file, line, kind and location.

line.description: 1-based. For JSON files, the first line where the value occurs; null when it does not occur.

kind.description: Id of the content rule in data/secret-patterns.json, or generic-assignment.

masked.description: The value as mask() shows it, for example sk-ant-…3f9a.

location.description: text (memory, rules, skills, commands, subagents), env.KEY (settings or a server), mcpServers.NAME.headers.KEY, mcpServers.NAME.env.KEY, or mcpServers.NAME.args[n].

envAtRoot.description: What the permission rules decide for a Read of .env at the root of the project.

preToolUseReadHooks.description: Each PreToolUse hook whose matcher covers Read, in the order of claudeConfig.hooks.

runsForEnv.description: Whether the hook runs for a Read of .env at the root.

claudeConfig.description: The Claude Code configuration of the target, read but never run. Every array is sorted. Strings from the target are redacted; env and header values are never copied.

settings.description: One item per settings file present.

parsed.description: False when the file is not a JSON object.

hooks.description: One item per hook handler. The command is read, never run.

if.description: The permission rule that filters the calls the hook runs for (docs: hooks), or null.

script.description: The script the command runs. Checked for existence only when it lies inside the project.

injectsContext.description: True for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion and PostModelSwitch.

subagents.description: One item per .claude/agents/**/*.md file, with tools, disallowedTools and permissionMode as written.

mcpServers.description: One item per server of .mcp.json. Keys of env and headers are listed by name only.

structure.description: The structure of the target: the folder tree, how far the memory maps it, the large files and the generated files, and the tools that enforce rules. Only file names and sizes come from the file list; no file is opened. Each large and generated entry says what the permission rules decide for Read and Edit, and whether the memory marks it as not to touch. Heuristics and thresholds are in scripts/lib/structure.mjs.

enforcementTools.description: Config files of tools that enforce rules: files at the root found by name, the workflows directly inside .github/workflows, and one entry for the .husky folder when it has files. Sorted by tool, then path.

path.description: Relative to the target, with forward slashes. The husky entry is the folder .husky.

tree.description: One entry per top-level folder and per second-level folder, built from the file list. files counts the files below the folder at any depth, generated ones included. Sorted by path. Files directly in the root are not counted.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target, without a trailing slash.

mapCoverage.description: Which top-level folders the memory maps. Only the folders that are not generated are counted. Memory files marked not-loaded are not read for this.

dirs.description: Number of top-level folders counted (the length of byDir).

mentioned.description: Number of those folders that the memory mentions.

byDir.description: One item per counted folder, sorted by dir.

files.description: Files below the folder, at any depth.

mentions.description: At most one entry per memory file: the first line of that file that mentions the folder. Sorted by file, then line.

file.description: Memory file, relative to the target.

largeFiles.description: Versioned files above THRESHOLDS.largeFileBytes (262,144 bytes, 256 KiB; provisional), sorted by path. Lockfiles (by base name, in any folder) and files of a generated entry are left out. When more than 200 are found, the first 200 by path are listed and a warning with reason large-files-cut gives the count that were cut.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target.

generatedFiles.description: Generated files and folders, sorted by path. A folder whose name is a pattern of data/generated-patterns.json is one entry at its outermost level, with every file below it; a file matching a file pattern is one entry. When more than 200 are found, the first 200 by path are listed and a warning with reason generated-entries-cut gives the count that were cut.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target. A folder has no trailing slash.

pattern.description: Id of the pattern of data/generated-patterns.json that matched.

files.description: Files in the entry: one for a file, every file below for a folder.

bytes.description: Total size of the files in the entry.

verification.description: How the target checks its work. The scripts come from the root package.json, read as data; the command text is not output.

commands.description: Scripts of the root package.json that run a check, sorted by name. A script with no category is not listed.

categories.description: Sorted. Set by the script name and by the command text.

mentioned.description: Calls that the memory files make to a listed script, in inline code and fenced blocks. Sorted by file, line and script.

text.description: The call as written, from the manager on.

code.description: Source code of the target, read as data by the duplication measure. Only paths, line numbers and counts are written, never code text. The caps, the line rules and the window length are in scripts/lib/duplication.mjs.

duplication.description: Blocks of normalized lines (no blank lines, comments, imports or punctuation-only lines) that repeat between files or inside one file. A group is a block with two or more copies, and it is listed only when it adds a redundant line that no group before it in the list already counts. Test files are only in inTests. When the file cap or the byte cap cuts files, a warning with reason code-files-cut or code-bytes-cut gives the count that were cut.

windowLines.description: Length of a window, in normalized lines. Every group is at least this long.

filesScanned.description: Main code files that were read and normalized. Test files and skipped files are not counted.

linesScanned.description: Normalized lines of the main files.

redundantLines.description: Normalized lines of the main files that are not the first copy of a group. A line that several groups mark is counted once.

duplicatedLinesPct.description: redundantLines divided by linesScanned, times 100, rounded to two decimals. 0 when nothing was scanned.

groupCount.description: Number of listed groups, before the listing is cut to the first ones.

groups.description: The first groups of the main files: most redundant lines first, then by the file and line of the first copy. At most MAX_GROUPS items.

redundantLines.description: lines multiplied by the number of copies minus one.

copies.description: Sorted by file, then by line. The first copy is not redundant.

file.description: POSIX path relative to the target.

line.description: Original line of the first normalized line of the copy.

endLine.description: Original line of the last normalized line of the copy.

inTests.description: The same numbers and groups, computed over the test files only (folders such as test, tests, __tests__, spec, e2e, __mocks__ and fixtures, or names such as *.test.* and *.spec.*).

filesScanned.description: Test code files that were read and normalized.

linesScanned.description: Normalized lines of the test files.

redundantLines.description: Redundant normalized lines of the test files.

duplicatedLinesPct.description: redundantLines divided by linesScanned, times 100, rounded to two decimals. 0 when nothing was scanned.

groupCount.description: Number of groups among the test files.

groups.description: The same shape and order as the main groups.

redundantLines.description: lines multiplied by the number of copies minus one.

copies.description: Sorted by file, then by line. The first copy is not redundant.

file.description: POSIX path relative to the target.

line.description: Original line of the first normalized line of the copy.

endLine.description: Original line of the last normalized line of the copy.

measurementRef.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer into this file. The scanner writes only keys and array indexes, so no escape is needed. The value it names exists in the same measurements.json.

evidence.description: A place in the target that the finding cites. file is a POSIX path relative to the target (a folder when the entry is a folder, or a settings or hook file that holds the harness setting). line and endLine are present only for a copy or a memory line that has them.

trigger.description: One reason for a finding. trigger is a fixed kebab-case name of the case that matched. impact is the impact of this trigger. threshold is present when the trigger compares a number with a THRESHOLDS key (key and its value, provisional). detail holds small facts that the trigger needs, such as the command ids that pass through an allow entry, or the decisions of a folder; it never holds code text.

measuredFinding.description: A finding of a measured rule. Its axis is the axis of its rule prefix. The impact is the highest impact of its triggers.

candidate.description: Something the agent must read for a judgment rule. kind selects the other fields: duplication-group has lines, redundantLines and copies (file, line, endLine; never code text); hook-script and memory-file have file; memory-file has loadMode (always, on-demand, not-loaded or null for a rule that could not be read).

verdict.description: What the permission rules decide for one Read (docs: permissions). rule and source are null when no rule decides.

protection.description: What the permission rules decide for one tool (Read or Edit) on an entry. A file gives its own verdict. A folder gives the verdict of its files when they all agree; when the rules differ but the decision is the same, rule and source are null and reason is several-rules; when the decisions differ, decision is mixed and counts gives the number of files per decision.

reason.description: Fixed code from permissions.mjs, or several-rules or several-decisions (structure only).

counts.description: Only when decision is mixed: the number of files with each decision. Undeterminable files are counted, never guessed.

entryMemory.description: The memory lines that name an entry (its path, or for a folder its path with a slash; for a file also its pattern glob), in file and line order. marked is true when one of those lines also contains a do-not-touch phrase from data/generated-patterns.json. A heuristic: the memory text is data.

file.description: Memory file, relative to the target.

markdownItem.description: A skill, command or subagent. loadMode always: its description is in the budget; not-loaded: disable-model-invocation, or a subagent without a name; null: the frontmatter could not be read.

descriptionChars.description: Length of description and when_to_use together.
